topics.label: Introduction and Framing of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the overarching framework for exploring cancer development through clonal evolution, cell of origin, and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Dynamics in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells acquire growth advantages through Darwinian clonal selection of driver mutations and non-mutational epigenetic chromatin remodeling.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell hypothesis and investigate how the cell of origin dictates transformation potential in leukemia and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Promotion of Tumor Outgrowth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how external environmental insults and chronic inflammation provide essential promotional cues that activate stem-like programs in mutated cells.

topics.label: Established Microenvironments, Profiling Technologies, and Coevolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine stromal dependency in established tumors, the modern single-cell and spatial methods used to map microenvironments, and an overarching synthesis of cancer coevolution.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Outlook
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapy.
